stories.label: Leaders of Russian 'Rybar' hybrid network Mikhail and Valeriia Zvinchuk arrested in Risan
stories.summary: Montenegro arrested Mikhail Zvinchuk, founder of Rybar, a pro-Kremlin military Telegram channel with about 1.5 million subscribers and reported ties to Russian intelligence, along with Valeriia Zvinchuk, in the coastal town of Risan, after officials warned of attempts to destabilise the country. Lead with the arrest and the charge or legal basis as the reports give it. The mechanism: say what Rybar is and how a blog became an instrument of state influence, what Montenegrin authorities say the pair were doing in a NATO member and EU candidate, and what Moscow's foreign ministry said in reply. Every allegation of intelligence ties is an allegation, attributed. Write from the Guardian, Meduza, Ukrainska Pravda and the Montenegrin outlet CdM; RT is Russian state media and is used only for Moscow's response. Write your own headline. Dateline Risan, or Podgorica if the reports file from there.

stories.label: Christa Pike's botched execution is a reminder of the horror of the death penalty | Moira Donegan
stories.summary: Tennessee tried to execute Christa Pike by lethal injection and failed; she survived. Lead with what happened in the chamber, as the BBC news report gives it: how long the attempt lasted, what went wrong, and her condition now. The mechanism: say which drug the state uses (pentobarbital is tagged) and where it gets it, what the execution protocol requires and where it broke down, what her lawyers are asking the courts for, and whether the state says it will try again. The accountability point: a state claimed the power to kill and could not carry it out competently, and say how often lethal injections have failed, only as the reports do. Name her victim and the crime in one sentence, with the same care. Write from the BBC; the Guardian page is an opinion column and the Aol page a family interview, so use them only for facts they attribute. The feed title is the column's: write your own. Dateline Nashville, or the prison town the BBC gives. US dateline (1 of 3).

stories.label: Iran proposes plan on shrinking water level in Caspian Sea
stories.summary: The heads of the Caspian littoral states held an extraordinary environmental summit over the sea's falling water level, and Iranian president Masoud Pezeshkian proposed a long-term regional programme to address it. Lead with the summit and why it was called: the world's largest lake is shrinking, with the figures only as the report gives them. The mechanism: say what is driving the fall (the report's own account of river inflow and climate), what Pezeshkian proposed and whether the other four states (Russia, Kazakhstan, Turkmenistan, Azerbaijan) agreed to anything, and who it lands on: ports, fisheries and coastal towns on five shores. A proposal is a proposal; state no decision the page does not report. Mehr is Iranian state media and the only source, so attribute throughout ('Iran's state-run Mehr news agency reported'). The same summit week was covered 10-09 for Putin's offer to Pezeshkian: one clause at most. Dateline Ashgabat, if the report places the summit there.

stories.label: How Houthi military aggression in Red Sea threatens Africa
stories.summary: Yemen's Houthis have seized territory at the entrance to the Red Sea since the February US-Israeli attack on Iran, and their growing ties with al-Shabaab in Somalia could carry the war across the Bab el-Mandeb into the Horn of Africa, Premium Times reports. Write it as a report of what the piece documents, not as commentary: lead with the most concrete finding (weapons, drones or training passing between the two groups, and who says so). The mechanism: say what each side gets from the other, what the Houthis now hold at the strait, and what it means for Somalia, Djibouti and the African economies whose trade passes through. Name the series plainly: ship traffic through Bab el-Mandeb. Attribute every claim of a link to the body that made it (UN monitors, researchers), and if the page is a republished analysis, name its original publisher. Premium Times is the regional outlet and the only source. Dateline Mogadishu, or the city the piece files from.

stories.label: Iran and Oman agree on 'safe route' in Hormuz
stories.summary: Iran and Oman agreed on a 'safe route' for ships through the Strait of Hormuz on the day Donald Trump ruled out new attacks on Iran until after the November midterms and said talks with Tehran were 'productive'. Lead with the route: who may use it, on whose terms, and who polices it, as The New Arab gives it. The mechanism: say what the agreement changes for tankers after two months of attacks and traffic at a two-month low (covered 10-08, one clause), what Iran's foreign ministry said, what Trump's post commits him to and what it does not, and how the oil price moved on it. Name the series plainly: ship traffic through the Strait of Hormuz and the price of Brent crude. Who it lands on: the Gulf exporters and the importing economies paying above $100 a barrel. This follows the 10-09 piece on Pezeshkian confirming talks with Washington (one clause). Write from The New Arab; the Middle East Eye page is a live-blog entry and the CoinDesk page a bitcoin recap, used only for Trump's words. Dateline Muscat, or Tehran if the report files from there.

stories.label: IRGC reports strike on gas tanker in Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps navy says it struck the MT Sunshine, a large liquefied-gas tanker, in the Strait of Hormuz, Russian state news agency TASS reported. Lead with the claim as a claim: who says they hit what, where and when, and that no shipowner, flag state or maritime-security agency is cited confirming it unless the page does. The mechanism: say what reason the IRGC gave (the vessel's route, flag or cargo), what is known of the ship, its cargo and crew, and how this sits against Iran's statement this week that routes outside its own will be closed, hours after Tehran and Muscat announced a 'safe route' (covered this cycle, one clause). Name the series plainly: ship traffic through the Strait of Hormuz and the price of natural gas. Who it lands on: the crew first, then LNG and LPG buyers in Asia. TASS is state media and the only source, so attribute every sentence and state nothing as fact. Dateline as TASS gives the incident's location; not Tunis, where the TASS item is filed.

stories.label: Hurricane Isaias Nears Florida as Second Storm Threatens West
stories.summary: Hurricane Isaias strengthened to a Category 3 storm with 120 mph (193 km/h) winds as it bore down on more than 3 million people along the US Gulf Coast, after forcing energy producers to curb output. Lead with the people in its path and the evacuation orders, then the forecast landfall and storm surge, attributed to the National Hurricane Center. The mechanism for the economy reader: say how much Gulf oil and gas production and refining has been shut in, as the reports give it, and why that matters in a week when Brent is already above $100 on the war around Hormuz. Name the series plainly: WTI crude and the price of natural gas. Give no damage or death figures the reports do not; it had not made landfall when they were written. Bloomberg may not fetch: write from Al Jazeera and the US News live file. Dateline the Florida or Alabama city the reports file from. US dateline (2 of 3).

stories.label: Trump's Fed ex-nominee Shelton to advise Bessent, Treasury says
stories.summary: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has hired Judy Shelton, Donald Trump's former pick for the Federal Reserve Board, as an adviser focused on China, the Treasury said. Lead with the appointment and the brief. The mechanism: say who Shelton is and why the Senate did not confirm her to the Fed, what she has argued about currencies and the dollar's link to gold, only as Reuters gives it, and what a China-focused adviser at Treasury works on now: the yuan's exchange rate, which the EU pressed Beijing over this week (covered 10-08, one clause), and trade talks. Name the series plainly: the yuan. It is a staffing decision, not a policy change: say what she can and cannot decide. Single wire source. Dateline Washington. US dateline (3 of 3).

stories.label: Nearly 1 in 10 young adults could have fatty, narrow arteries | New Scientist
stories.summary: Nearly one in ten younger adults already has plaque in their arteries, according to a study of almost 17,000 people reported by New Scientist. Lead with the proportion and the age range it covers. The mechanism: say how the plaque was detected (which scan), where the participants came from (Finland and Spain are tagged) and how representative they are, which risk factors separated those with plaque from those without, and what the researchers and outside cardiologists say it means for screening, which now starts in middle age. State the limits as the piece does: plaque seen on a scan is not a heart attack, and say whether the study followed anyone over time. Name the journal and lead author if the page does. Single specialist source. Give the article a dateline and location: the city of the lead institution as the report gives it.

stories.label: India rejects monopoly claim after Musk accuses Ambani of blocking Starlink launch
stories.summary: New since the 10-08 piece on India defending its satellite-internet approval process (one clause): Elon Musk has now named Mukesh Ambani, suggesting the owner of Jio is using political influence to block Starlink's launch, and India's telecom minister answered on Friday that the country 'does not allow a monopoly in any sector'. Lead with the accusation and the reply. The mechanism: say which approvals Starlink still lacks and who grants them, how satellite spectrum is being allocated (administratively or by auction) and why Jio and Starlink want opposite answers, what Jio's share of India's mobile market is, and what the opposition (Rahul Gandhi is tagged) made of it. An accusation is an accusation: Musk's claim is his, and say whether Reliance responded. Who it matters to: the rural users neither fibre nor towers reach. Write from Reuters; RT is Russian state media and is used only where it agrees. Dateline New Delhi; Reuters files from Bengaluru.

stories.label: Italy Explores Building an Artificial Gravity Research Platform in Orbit
stories.summary: The Italian Space Agency (ASI) said on 8 October that it is exploring an orbital platform that generates artificial gravity for research, and will open a consultation with scientists and industry later this month. Lead with what is proposed and say at once what it is: a study and a call for ideas, not a funded programme. The mechanism for a technical reader: say how the platform would produce gravity (rotation, and at what radius and rate if the page gives them), what partial gravity lets researchers test that the space station cannot (the range between weightlessness and Earth, where the Moon and Mars sit), who would build it and on what timeline, and what nobody has yet flown. The wider point: with the International Space Station nearing retirement, national agencies are staking out what replaces it. Single specialist source. Dateline Rome.

stories.label: As U.S. blocks DJI, Insta360 races to win American creators
stories.summary: With DJI shut out of the US market, the smaller Chinese camera maker Insta360 and its independent drone brand Antigravity are moving to take its customers, Rest of World reports. Lead with the opening and who is filling it: one Chinese company's ban has become another's market. The mechanism: say what the US restriction on DJI actually is and why Insta360 is not caught by it, how Antigravity is structured to stay clear, what share and sales figures the piece gives, and how exposed the company remains to the same rule being widened. The structural point: a ban aimed at a country's technology ends up choosing among that country's firms. The feed entry was a one-line teaser: write only what the page supports. Single specialist source. Dateline Shenzhen, where Insta360 is based, unless the report files from elsewhere.

stories.label: South Africa's Navanethem 'Navi' Pillay wins 2026 Nobel Peace Prize
stories.summary: The Norwegian Nobel Committee gave the 2026 Peace Prize to Navi Pillay, 85, the South African judge, 'for her efforts to promote peace and international law'. Lead with the award and the committee's own words, then what she actually did, as the reports give it: the Rwanda tribunal bench, the International Criminal Court, UN human rights chief, and the UN commission of inquiry on the occupied Palestinian territory, whose genocide finding is why the feed tags the word; state that finding exactly as the reports do and attribute it. The mechanism: a prize for international law in a year when the courts that apply it are under sanction and attack, so say which governments welcomed it and which objected, each attributed. Hindustan Times adds her grandparents were Indian indentured labourers in Natal; one clause. Al-Monitor carries the Reuters text. Dateline Oslo.

stories.label: South Africa pulls asylum directive after violent protests
stories.summary: South Africa's Department of Home Affairs withdrew a directive telling its offices to accept asylum applications and judge them on their merits, after anti-immigrant protests turned violent in Durban and Soweto. Lead with the reversal and who it lands on: asylum seekers who can again be turned away on procedural grounds before anyone hears their case. The mechanism: say what the directive said and which court ruling it answered (the Constitutional Court is tagged), who organised the protests and what was attacked, how many were hurt or arrested, and what misinformation about the directive circulated, as the reports give it. The structural point: a government dropped a measure its own courts required because of street violence. Daily Maverick's report from Friday morning has the director-general's withdrawal and the local detail: https://www.dailymaverick.co.za/article/2026-10-09-home-affairs-scraps-asylum-seeker-directive-after-violence-in-durban-and-soweto/ . Dateline Johannesburg, or Pretoria if the reports file the decision from there.

stories.label: Trump envoys pitching 'new ideas' to settle Ukraine conflict - media -- RT World News
stories.summary: The new development since the Kramatorsk bus-stop bombing (covered 10-08, one clause; the toll is now at least 35 in the Guardian): Volodymyr Zelenskyy publicly accused the United States of being unwilling to help Ukraine, while Trump's envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner met Ukrainian negotiators and, Axios reports via Meduza, carry 'new ideas' and plan to go to Moscow this month. Lead with that collision: the president of the country being bombed says Washington will not help on the day Washington's envoys say they have a plan. The mechanism: say what Zelenskyy asked for (wider Starlink access to target ballistic-missile launchers) and why that is in one company's and one government's gift, what is known of the envoys' ideas and what is not, and what Kyiv and Moscow each said. Write from the Guardian, the Reuters text on Yahoo, Ukrainska Pravda and Meduza; RT is Russian state media and is used only where the independent reports agree. The feed title is RT's; write your own. Dateline Kyiv.

stories.label: 3 killed in Saudi Arabia after Houthi attack on Riyadh airport
stories.summary: The new development since the 10-08 piece on the second day of strikes and the oil price (one clause): Yemen's Houthis now say a ballistic missile hit Riyadh's airport and badly damaged a plane, and airlines have begun suspending flights to the Saudi capital. Lead with the suspensions, which are verifiable, then the claim, marked as a claim: Saudi Arabia has not commented on it and has confirmed only the three killed in the airport strikes earlier this week, so do not present the three dead as a result of this latest strike. The mechanism: say which airlines stopped flying and for how long, what a closed or half-closed Riyadh means for a Gulf already cut off by sea, what the Houthis say they are answering (the coalition's air campaign in Yemen, including the Sanaa school-bus strike covered 10-08, one clause), and what Saudi air defences did. Count the dead on both sides with the authority that gave each figure. Dawn is the regional outlet in the cluster; no Saudi or Gulf outlet carried it. Dateline Riyadh.

stories.label: Zack Polanski faces greatest crisis of his leadership so far
stories.summary: Sagal Abdi-Wali, who arrived in Britain as a child refugee from Somalia in the 1990s and grew up in Camden, won the Holborn and St Pancras by-election in north London. Lead with the result, not the BBC's leadership-crisis frame: who won, for which party, by what margin and on what turnout, and why the seat was vacant, each as the reports give it; state nothing about party or margin that the pages do not. The mechanism: the Greens under Zack Polanski had been expected to take the seat, so say what went wrong for them, what the result says about Labour and Keir Starmer, and why Andy Burnham is in the story. Who it matters to: a Somali-born Muslim woman now holds one of the most watched seats in British politics; Al Jazeera's pre-vote report says what the campaign was fought on, Gaza included if it says so. The New York Times may be paywalled. Dateline London.

stories.label: Russia ready to help Iran resolve conflict with US-Israel: Putin
stories.summary: Vladimir Putin told Iranian president Masoud Pezeshkian on Thursday that Moscow is ready to help resolve Iran's conflict with the United States and Israel, and Pezeshkian confirmed that talks with Washington will continue. Lead with Pezeshkian's confirmation, which is the news: after a week of reports that the Pentagon was drafting strike options before the US midterms (covered 10-08, one clause), Tehran says the channel is open. The mechanism: say where they met (the Commonwealth of Independent States summit; Turkmenistan is tagged), what Putin actually offered and whether anyone accepted it, what format the US-Iran talks take and who mediates them, and what Russia gains from the role. An offer is an offer: no agreement was announced. Single source, an Indian outlet carrying agency copy; Mehr, Iranian state media, reports Pezeshkian at the same summit (https://en.mehrnews.com/news/248436/Pezeshkian-stresses-expansion-of-Armenia-ties-in-all-fields) and may be used for the venue only. Dateline the summit city as the report gives it.

stories.label: India Scraps Key Tax Relief for Gold Imports, Raising Costs
stories.summary: India let a tax exemption on banks' imports of gold, silver and platinum lapse, and banks have been paying a 3% integrated goods and services tax on bullion since April, the revenue secretary confirmed. Lead with the odd part: the world's second-largest gold buyer raised the cost of importing it six months ago and it is only now public. The mechanism: say what the relief was, how the 3% tax works (paid up front at import, recoverable later, so it ties up banks' capital), who it lands on (the banks that bring in bullion, then jewellers and households for whom gold is savings), and why the government did it: to curb imports and protect the rupee and the trade balance, only as the reports say. Name the series plainly: the price of gold. Give the gold price and India's import volumes only as Reuters gives them. Bloomberg may not fetch; write from Reuters. Dateline Mumbai.

stories.label: Brazil's Bolsonaro Promises a Sharp Pivot on Climate and the Amazon
stories.summary: New since the 10-08 piece on Flávio Bolsonaro's pension pledge (one clause): the front-runner in Brazil's 25 October runoff against President Lula is promising to reverse course on climate and the Amazon, and Reuters reports that the tight race has put Brazil's climate-finance push in doubt. Lead with the money and the forest: which funds and commitments depend on who wins (the forest-finance facility Brazil has been raising money for, the Amazon Fund, donor pledges, each only as the reports name them), and what Bolsonaro says he would do about enforcement and deforestation targets. The mechanism: donors and investors commit against a government's policy, so a credible chance of reversal freezes money before a vote is cast; give the deforestation figures under each previous government only as the reports do. Al Jazeera adds that a Supreme Court judge issued an arrest warrant for his brother Eduardo Bolsonaro: one sentence, attributed. A campaign promise is a promise. Bloomberg may not fetch; write from Reuters and Al Jazeera. The Hindu page is a video of student protests. Dateline Brasília, or the city Reuters files from.

stories.label: Factcheck: UK Conservatives double the ‘cost of net-zero’ after spreadsheet blunder
stories.summary: A booklet published by Britain's opposition Conservative Party puts a 'cost of net-zero' figure at the centre of its case against climate policy, and Carbon Brief's analysis finds the number appears to have been doubled by a spreadsheet error. Lead with the two numbers: what the booklet claims and what the same sources give when the sum is done correctly. The mechanism for a numerate reader: say exactly what the error was (what was counted twice, or which column was added to which), where the underlying figures come from, and what a gross cost leaves out, such as the fuel not bought; then what the party said when asked. The structural point: a headline number that will be repeated through an election cycle rests on arithmetic nobody checked before publication. Attribute the finding to Carbon Brief and use its 'appears to' where it does. Single specialist source. Dateline London.

stories.label: We're still figuring out the side effects of GLP-1 weight-loss drugs
stories.summary: Research presented this week at an ageing meeting in Boston found that overweight and diabetic people taking GLP-1 drugs score younger on at least some measures of biological age, MIT Technology Review reports, alongside a still-growing list of side effects. Lead with the finding and its size, stated exactly as the page does, and say at once what it is: a conference presentation, not a published trial. The mechanism: say what 'biological age' measures here (which clock or biomarker), whether the effect is separable from weight loss itself, who ran the study and in how many people, and then what the page reports on side effects and what remains unknown. The page is a weekly column: take the findings and their sources from it and leave out the first-person framing. Who it matters to: these drugs are taken by tens of millions and priced out of reach in most of the world. Give the article a dateline and location: Boston, where the research was presented. US dateline (1 of 3).

stories.label: MARA transfers $81.1 million in bitcoin (BTC) to Galaxy Digital as strategy pivots to AI
stories.summary: MARA Holdings, one of the largest bitcoin miners, moved about 996 BTC ($81m) to an address identified as Galaxy Digital's, after cutting its holdings by 18,245 BTC between February and August to pay down debt and build AI computing infrastructure. Lead with the larger number, not the day's transfer: a company whose business was accumulating bitcoin has been selling it to become a data-centre operator. The mechanism for a technical reader: a miner's real assets are power contracts, grid connections and cooled buildings, which AI computing now pays more for than mining does; say what MARA is building and for whom, what the shift does to the network's hash rate and to who is left mining, and that the destination address is an attribution by a chain-analytics firm, not a company statement. Name the series plainly: the price of bitcoin, in one clause, with no price commentary. Single specialist source. Give the article a dateline and location: the city of MARA's headquarters as CoinDesk gives it. US dateline (2 of 3).

stories.label: Co-creator of Empire Market dark web marketplace given 40-year sentence
stories.summary: Raheim Hamilton, 30, co-creator of the Empire Market dark-web marketplace, was sentenced to 40 years in a US prison after pleading guilty to a drug conspiracy charge and agreeing to forfeit more than $100m in bitcoin and several properties in Virginia. Lead with the sentence and the forfeiture. The mechanism for a technical reader: say what Empire Market was and how large (listings, users, sales volume, as The Record gives them), how it operated (Tor, cryptocurrency escrow) and how it ended, how investigators identified its operators and traced the bitcoin, and what happened to the co-defendant. The point worth a sentence: 40 years for running the platform rather than selling on it sets the going rate for marketplace operators. Give nothing the page does not; the feed entry was a two-line teaser. Single specialist source. Dateline the city of the sentencing court as The Record gives it. US dateline (3 of 3). The feed's pubDate is in the future (10 October, 00:55 GMT): check it against the page.

stories.label: ICE agent shoots man in New York City
stories.summary: A federal immigration agent shot a man in Marble Hill, New York, reportedly in a car with a five-year-old child inside; Mayor Zohran Mamdani called it 'unconscionable' and demanded the man's release, and protests followed in the Bronx. Lead with the shooting and the man's condition, then who says what: the mayor, the Department of Homeland Security's account of why the agent fired, and the police department's role, each attributed, since the versions differ (Fox frames him as an illegal immigrant, the mayor as a victim). The mechanism: a city government has no command over federal agents operating on its streets, so say what New York can and cannot do (investigate, prosecute, refuse cooperation) and who investigates a federal agent's use of force. Name the man if the reports do. Dateline New York. US dateline (1 of 3).

stories.label: Two Latvian men arrested inside UK military base after breach
stories.summary: British counterterrorism police arrested two Latvian nationals, aged 32 and 36, inside RAF Molesworth, the Cambridgeshire base that houses major US and NATO intelligence operations, days after British authorities alleged an Iran-linked plot at RAF Fairford, another American airbase. Lead with the breach: how far in they got, what they are suspected of and under which law they are held. The mechanism: say what Molesworth does (intelligence analysis for US and NATO commands), who guards a US-used base on British soil, and what links, if any, police draw to the Fairford case; state no motive or sponsor the reports do not give, and treat the Iran allegation as an allegation. The structural point: US bases in Britain are being used in a war with Iran and have become targets, while their perimeter security has failed twice in a week (the B-1B's retreat from a UK airbase was covered 10-08, one clause). Write from Al Jazeera, which carries the Reuters reporting; RT is Russian state media and is used only where it agrees with it. Dateline Molesworth.

stories.label: Mexico prison clash in strife-torn Sinaloa state leaves 10 dead
stories.summary: Ten people were killed and 16 injured in a fight inside the El Castillo penitentiary in Mazatlán, Sinaloa, state authorities said. Lead with the dead (nine inmates and the tenth as the report identifies them) and attribute the count to the Sinaloa Public Security Secretariat. The mechanism: say what weapons were used and how they got inside, who the authorities say fought whom, how security forces retook the prison, and how this sits inside the two-year war between the Chapitos and Mayiza factions of the Sinaloa Cartel (covered 10-08 from Culiacán, one clause), in which prisons hold members of both sides. The structural point: the state cannot keep order inside a building it runs. Give earlier prison killings in Sinaloa only if the report does. Single source; no Latin American outlet in the feed. The feed's concept tags include Rio de Janeiro and unrelated Spanish entries: ignore them. Dateline Mazatlán.

stories.label: Forgotten schoolchildren of Borno
stories.summary: Nearly six months after insurgents seized dozens of students from a school in Borno State, the children are still held and the abduction has dropped out of national attention, Premium Times reports. Lead with the number taken, the school and town, the date, and how many remain in captivity, each as the report gives it. The mechanism: say which group took them, what the federal and state governments have done and said since (rescue attempts, negotiations, ransom), what the families told the reporters, and how school abductions spread from one incident under Goodluck Jonathan through Muhammadu Buhari's years to a southward wave under Bola Tinubu, with the counts the report supplies. Who it lands on: the children and their parents, named where the piece names them, and a region where the risk of abduction keeps children out of school. Write it as a report of what was found, not as commentary. Premium Times is the regional outlet and the only source. Dateline the Borno town the report names (Maiduguri if it files from there).

stories.label: US pressured EU to withdraw sponsorship of disinformation conference
stories.summary: The European Union withdrew its sponsorship of a disinformation conference in Lithuania on the day it opened, after pressure from Washington over a panel titled 'USA as a FIMI threat: adapt, acknowledge, push back' (FIMI is foreign information manipulation and interference). Lead with the withdrawal and the panel title. The mechanism: say who in the US government objected and through what channel, what reason the EU gave in public (concerns about the framing), what the organisers and panellists say, and whether the panel went ahead. Attribute the claim of US pressure to whoever makes it and on what evidence (documents, named officials, anonymous sources); if the page is a republished wire or partner report, name the original reporter. The structural point: the EU built its counter-disinformation apparatus against Russia and China and dropped its name from an event the moment the same lens was turned on its ally. Single source carried by a Nigerian outlet. Dateline Vilnius.

stories.label: Two tech outsiders tried to sell a $44bn tech company. It didn't work
stories.summary: Firmus, the Nvidia-backed AI data-centre company, has scrapped what would have been one of Australia's biggest-ever stock market listings, at a valuation of about $44bn, citing 'recent market volatility and prevailing market conditions'. Lead with the cancelled listing and the valuation, and say in which currency. The mechanism: say what Firmus actually owns and earns against what it promised to build, who its founders are and why the Sydney Morning Herald calls them outsiders, what Nvidia's stake is, how much it sought to raise and why investors balked, and what it means for data centres already under construction. The wider point: this week's selloff after OpenAI's weaker revenue is now closing the public market to AI infrastructure companies that need it to fund their building, the other side of the boom behind Samsung's record profit (covered 10-08, one clause). Dateline Sydney, or the city the reports give for the company.

stories.label: FG to negotiate ₦1,350 petrol price ceiling as global oil shock drives pump prices
stories.summary: Nigeria's federal government says it is negotiating a ceiling of ₦1,350 a litre on the ex-gantry or landing cost of petrol, as the price of Brent crude, driven above $100 by the war around the Strait of Hormuz, pushes pump prices up in Africa's largest oil producer. Lead with the ceiling and what Nigerians pay at the pump now. The mechanism: say which minister announced it and who is on the other side of the negotiation (the Dangote refinery and importers), why a crude exporter imports the oil shock (refined product priced at world levels and in dollars, a weak naira), how a ceiling differs from the subsidy scrapped in 2023 and who would absorb the gap if costs rise above it. Name the series plainly: Brent crude and the naira. Who it lands on: households and transport operators for whom petrol sets the price of food and fares. It is a negotiation, not a decision: mark it as one. Premium Times is the regional outlet and the only source. Dateline Abuja.

stories.label: India's TCS rises on AI revenue, international business growth
stories.summary: Tata Consultancy Services, India's largest IT services company, reported second-quarter results showing faster AI-related revenue and growth abroad, and its shares rose about 5%, lifting the whole Indian IT index. Lead with the results, not the share price: revenue, net profit and the AI figure in rupees with the year-on-year change, as Reuters and Mint give them. The mechanism: India's $315bn software services industry sells labour by the hour to Western clients, the business AI was expected to hollow out, so say what TCS counts as AI revenue, what happened to headcount, and where the international growth came from. Then the tension the reader should see: this week the US administration suspended green card sponsorship for firms including Tata (covered 10-08, one clause), and the industry's largest market is restricting the people it sends there. Skip the buy-sell-hold commentary in Goodreturns; use it only for the dividend. Dateline Mumbai.

stories.label: Chinese developer makes ARTEX AI agent closed-source after Korean bank hack
stories.summary: The Chinese developer of ARTEX, an open-source AI agent, has closed its source after security firms identified it as a tool used in a cyberattack campaign against South Korean banks. Lead with the decision and the developer's own words ('Given the misuse of the tool...'). The mechanism for a technical reader: say what ARTEX does (an autonomous agent, and which offensive steps the attackers had it perform), which firms made the identification (CrowdStrike is tagged) and what they found, what was taken from the banks, and whether anyone has attributed the campaign to a state or group, as an attribution and not as fact. Then the point developers will argue over: closing a repository does not recall the copies and forks already downloaded, so say what the move changes in practice and what it signals for dual-use agent tooling released in the open. Single wire source. Dateline Seoul, where Reuters files it.

stories.label: Alibaba sues Pentagon to denounce being classified as a Chinese military affiliate
stories.summary: Alibaba has sued the US Department of Defense over its placement on the Pentagon's list of Chinese military companies; the department's public document describes it as indirectly affiliated with the supervision body of China's State Council and as a 'military-civil fusion contributor to the Chinese defense industrial base'. Lead with the suit: the court, what Alibaba asks for and its central argument. The mechanism: say what the list is (the Section 1260H designation), what it does and does not do in law (no sanction by itself, but a bar on future Pentagon contracting and a signal that drives investors and partners away), on what evidence the Pentagon acted, and how earlier challenges ended, Xiaomi's removal in 2021 among them, only as the report gives it. The structural point: a cloud and e-commerce company with customers across Asia and the Gulf can be labelled a military entity on an 'indirect affiliation' standard that only a US court can test. Every claim in the complaint is an allegation. Single source. Dateline Washington. US dateline (2 of 3).

stories.label: SOL news: Solana is about to halve its block times as final 200-millisecond upgrade nears
stories.summary: Solana is due on Friday to cut the interval between blocks to 200 milliseconds, half the current time and the last in a series of staged reductions. Lead with the number and the date, and say it is scheduled, not done. The mechanism for a technical reader: say how the network gets there (the consensus and scheduling changes CoinDesk describes), what faster blocks buy (shorter confirmation delays, less room for the trading exploits that depend on the gap between blocks) and what they cost: more frequent validator votes, heavier demands on network links, and a shorter window in which a signed transaction stays valid, which can break wallets and applications that assumed the old timing. The structural question: whether hardware and bandwidth requirements that keep rising leave fewer operators able to run a validator. No price talk. Single specialist source. Give the article a dateline and location as CoinDesk does; if it gives none, use the city of the organisation that announced the schedule.

stories.label: 14-Year-Old Girl Riding Home on a School Bus Killed by Saudi Coalition Strike in Yemen
stories.summary: A Saudi-led coalition airstrike killed a 14-year-old girl on her school bus in Sanaa as Yemen's war between Ansarallah (the Houthis) and the Saudi-backed coalition reignites. Lead with the girl: her name, where the bus was, the date and the other dead and wounded, each as Drop Site documents it. Then the mechanism: what the coalition says it was aiming at, how many strikes have hit Sanaa since fighting resumed, who supplies the aircraft and munitions, and what the coalition has said about this strike, if anything. The site has covered this week's Houthi missile claims near Bab el-Mandeb and the strikes on Riyadh from the other side; this is the civilian cost in Yemen, counted with the same care. Attribute the strike as the piece does and state nothing it does not support. Single investigative source; no regional outlet in the feed. Dateline Sanaa.

stories.label: Armenia, Azerbaijan discuss stepping up search for war missing
stories.summary: Armenian prime minister Nikol Pashinyan said he and Azerbaijani president Ilham Aliyev discussed stepping up the search for people missing from three decades of war, as a conference in Baku ended with Azerbaijan detailing the information it has exchanged with Yerevan. Lead with the number of missing on each side, counted symmetrically and attributed (Azerbaijan's roughly 4,000 from the 1990s war, Armenia's missing from 2020 and 2023, as Reuters gives them). The mechanism: finding the dead needs each side to hand over maps of burial sites and minefields and to allow exhumation and DNA matching, so say what has been exchanged, what the Red Cross's role is, and what remains withheld, including the Armenian detainees still held in Baku if the report raises them. The structural point: two states that have initialled a peace deal are testing it on the one issue where families, not governments, keep the count. Single wire source; no regional outlet in the feed. Dateline Baku.

stories.label: Ekurhuleni police force employed convicted killers, Parliament told
stories.summary: Vetting of the Ekurhuleni Metropolitan Police Department, the municipal force of a city of four million east of Johannesburg, found 63 officials with criminal convictions before they were hired, murder among them, and 55 who picked up 72 convictions while serving, for violent crime, attempted murder, theft, fraud and firearm offences, South Africa's Parliament was told. Lead with those numbers. The mechanism: say how people with murder convictions passed recruitment, who was responsible for vetting and why it was done only now, what the parliamentary committee (Scopa is tagged) was told about financial write-offs alongside it, and what happens to the officers named: suspension, dismissal or nothing. The structural point: a force that carries state firearms and arrest powers was never checked against the state's own criminal records. This connects to the 10-07 piece on legal guns reaching criminals through police and private security (one clause). Single source, original reporting from the hearing. Dateline Cape Town, where Parliament sits, unless the page files from Ekurhuleni.

stories.label: Two Years On, the Sinaloa Cartel War Changes Shape | The InSight Take
stories.summary: Two years after Ismael 'El Mayo' Zambada was delivered to US authorities, the war it set off between the Chapitos and Mayiza factions of the Sinaloa Cartel has not ended; InSight Crime's reporters, back from interviewing drug producers and residents in Culiacán, found it less visible and no less present. Write it as a report of what they found, not as a retrospective: lead with the most concrete finding the page gives (deaths and disappearances over the two years, with their source, and what has changed on the streets). The mechanism: say how one arrest split a criminal organisation, how the fighting moved from open gun battles to something quieter (disappearances, extortion, control of production), what it has done to fentanyl and methamphetamine output as producers told the reporters, and what it means for criminal groups elsewhere in Mexico. Who it lands on: the people of Culiacán, named where the piece names them. The page may be mostly a video with a summary: write only what its text supports and keep it short if the text is short. Single investigative source. Dateline Culiacán.

stories.label: Oil prices surge after second day of Houthi strikes on Riyadh
stories.summary: Yemen's Houthis struck Riyadh for a second day, hitting the capital's airport and killing at least three people, and the price of Brent crude jumped on fear that the war is widening from the Strait of Hormuz to the Saudi heartland. Lead with the strike and the dead, then the price and how far it moved. The mechanism: say what was hit and what Saudi air defences stopped, what the Houthis say they were answering (the coalition's air campaign in Yemen, covered separately this cycle, one clause), how much oil Saudi Arabia exports and by which routes now that Iran has stepped up attacks on ships in Hormuz, and why a threat to Saudi territory moves the price more than another tanker does. Name the series plainly: the price of Brent crude and ship traffic through the Strait of Hormuz. Who it lands on: the people killed in Riyadh first, then every oil-importing economy already paying above $100 a barrel. Attribute casualty figures to the authority that gave them. Single source; no Saudi or regional outlet in the feed carried the strikes. Dateline Riyadh.

stories.label: Samsung expects 780% quarterly operating profit jump on AI boom
stories.summary: Samsung Electronics projected a third-quarter operating profit above 100 trillion won, which Reuters calls a world first for a technology company and a nearly nine-fold rise on a year earlier, on demand for the memory chips that AI data centres consume. Lead with the figure and what it is: preliminary guidance, not audited results. The mechanism: say why memory, not processors, is where the money now is (high-bandwidth memory stacked beside AI accelerators, and a shortage that has pushed up ordinary DRAM and NAND prices too), how much of the profit comes from the chip division, and the caveat News18 reports that chip margins may be flat from here. Who it lands on: the buyers of every phone, laptop and server that now costs more because memory does, and a South Korean economy whose exports lean on one company; this is the same AI-hardware boom the WTO credited for its raised trade forecast (covered 10-08, one clause). The Aol page carries the Reuters text. Dateline Seoul.

stories.label: Euro zone finance ministers start steps to replace ECB's Schnabel
stories.summary: Euro-zone finance ministers opened the process to replace Isabel Schnabel on the European Central Bank's six-member executive board; she leaves on 3 January for a post at the International Monetary Fund, and governments have until 28 October to name candidates. Lead with the vacancy and the deadline. The mechanism: say what the seat is (Schnabel runs the bank's market operations and has been its most influential voice for tighter policy), how a board member is chosen (Eurogroup recommendation, European Parliament hearing, leaders' appointment, a single eight-year term), which countries are expected to put names forward and what the informal rule is about large states holding seats, as Reuters gives it. Why it matters now: the ECB raised its policy rate in September and is expected to raise again in December with inflation near double its target (covered 10-08, one clause), so who replaces its leading hawk bears on the ECB's policy rate and on the euro. Name those series plainly. Single wire source. Dateline Brussels.

stories.label: Top Democrat among Senate investigators probes ties between Cantor Fitzgerald, Tether
stories.summary: Senator Richard Blumenthal, the senior Democrat on the Senate's Permanent Subcommittee on Investigations, has demanded answers about the ties between Cantor Fitzgerald and Tether, issuer of the world's largest stablecoin: Cantor holds and manages Tether's US reserves and the two share other business interests. Lead with the demand and what it asks for, and say plainly that it is a letter from the minority, not a subpoena. The mechanism: say what Tether's reserves are (mostly US Treasury bills, backing a dollar token used far more outside the United States than in it), what Cantor earns for holding them and what stake it has in Tether, and why the link is a conflict question: Cantor was run by Howard Lutnick until he became commerce secretary, and the administration writes the rules stablecoins operate under, only as CoinDesk reports it. Who it lands on: the people in Turkey, Nigeria, Argentina and elsewhere who hold savings in Tether because their own currency fails them, and who depend on reserves no regulator audits. Every allegation is an allegation; give Cantor's and Tether's replies. Single specialist source. Dateline Washington. US dateline (4 of 4: taken for the economy floor, see summary).

stories.label: 'Breathtaking,' 'Devastating': Mathematics Reels After New OpenAI Release
stories.summary: The new development since the 10-07 piece on researchers racing an AI to the 'Unique Games' proof (one clause): OpenAI has now published a release of mathematical results, and working mathematicians have answered it. Alex Kontorovich, who chairs mathematics at Rutgers, says that from a human it 'would be an instant Fields Medal'; Nature reports that at least twice in five weeks researchers have said an AI system reached a result they had spent a long period working towards. Lead with what the release actually contains, stated exactly: which problems, proved or only claimed, and whether the proofs have been checked by people or by a formal proof assistant; the feed tags the Millennium Prize Problems, so say precisely what relation the results bear to them and claim nothing the pages do not. The mechanism for a technical reader: how the system was run (autonomously or with mathematicians steering), what verification has been done and by whom, and what remains unverified. Then the consequence both reports turn on: what is left for a doctoral student or a research group when a result can be scooped by a machine, and who gets credit. Quote the sceptics as well as the stunned. The Times may be paywalled: write from Nature's news report and use the Times only for what the fetched page gives. Give the article a dateline and location: the city of the mathematician the reports lead with, not OpenAI's office.

stories.label: Chemists uncover the true active surface of nickel catalysts
stories.summary: A team at Ulm University reports in Nature Catalysis that the working surface of a nickel electrode in alkaline water electrolysis is nickel dioxide (NiO2), not the nickel oxyhydroxide (NiOOH) that textbooks and catalyst designers have assumed for decades. Lead with the overturned assumption. The mechanism for a technical reader: say what alkaline electrolysis is and why nickel matters to it (a cheap, robust alternative to the iridium and platinum that other electrolysers need), how the researchers observed the surface under real reaction conditions and with which technique, what distinguishes NiO2 from NiOOH chemically, and why the difference changes how one would design a better catalyst for the oxygen-evolution step, which is where electrolysers lose most of their efficiency. State the limits: what conditions the result was shown under and whether any improved catalyst has been made from it. Who it lands on: green hydrogen is priced by its electricity losses, and the countries betting on it include Morocco, Egypt, Saudi Arabia and Oman. Name the lead authors as the page does. Dateline Ulm.

stories.label: Judge weighs if Trump can charge $100K for early access to Truth Social posts
stories.summary: A federal judge will decide within weeks whether Donald Trump may sell early access to his Truth Social posts for $100,000, which would make him, as Ars puts it, the first president to profit personally from selling advance access to government information. Lead with the product and the price: who is offered the feed, how many seconds or minutes early, and through what interface (an API is tagged). The mechanism: a president's posts announce tariffs, sanctions and military decisions and move markets within seconds, so a paid head start is a tradable advantage; say who sued and on what law, what the Justice Department lawyer Brantley Mayers argued at Wednesday's hearing about why the posts are private speech and not official records, how the judge responded, and what order is sought. Accountability is the point: the line between a president's office and his company is being drawn by one district court. Every claim by the plaintiffs is an allegation; no ruling has been made. Single specialist source. Dateline Washington, or the court's city as Ars gives it. US dateline (1 of 3).

stories.label: Let's Encrypt cuts certificate lifetimes to 64 days starting February 2027
stories.summary: Let's Encrypt, the free certificate authority behind the HTTPS padlock on most of the web's sites, will cut the life of its TLS certificates from 90 days to 64 from 10 February 2027. Lead with the date and the number; the reader runs servers and needs to know whether anything breaks. The mechanism: say why shorter lifetimes are safer (a stolen or mis-issued certificate expires sooner, and revocation has never worked reliably), how renewal is meant to be automatic through the ACME protocol and what ARI (ACME Renewal Information) adds, which setups will fail (manual renewals, cron jobs timed to 60 or 90 days, embedded devices), and where this sits on the industry schedule set by the CA/Browser Forum towards 47-day certificates. The structural point: one non-profit's default now sets operating practice for hundreds of millions of sites, including every small publisher and mosque website that cannot pay for a certificate. Single specialist source. Give the article a dateline and location: San Francisco, where Let's Encrypt's parent, the Internet Security Research Group, is based. US dateline (2 of 3).

stories.label: R.I.P. Margaret Hamilton, whose code saved the Apollo 11 Moon landing
stories.summary: Margaret Hamilton, who led development of the on-board flight software for NASA's Apollo programme and coined the term 'software engineering', died last week aged 90. Write a news obituary, not a tribute: lead with the death and the one thing she built that mattered most. The mechanism for a technical reader: in the last minutes of the Apollo 11 descent the guidance computer was flooded with spurious radar data and raised the 1201 and 1202 alarms; the software her team at the MIT Instrumentation Laboratory had designed used priority scheduling to shed low-priority jobs and restart the essential ones, so the landing continued. Say what that design was (asynchronous, priority-driven, built to recover from errors its authors could not foresee), why she argued software deserved the discipline of engineering at a time when it was not budgeted or scheduled as such, and what she did afterwards, as Ars gives it. Give the date and place of death and the cause only if the page states them. The feed's concept tags are wrong (an actress, a Canadian city): ignore them. Single specialist source. Dateline as Ars gives it, otherwise Cambridge, Massachusetts. US dateline (3 of 3).

stories.label: Trump bars Microsoft from US green card scheme
stories.summary: The Trump administration has suspended Microsoft, Adobe and several other large IT firms from sponsoring foreign staff for permanent residency, accusing them of replacing American employees with overseas workers; MoneyControl reports Infosys, Wipro and Tata are also targeted. Lead with the suspension: which programme exactly (the green card labour-certification route, as distinct from the H-1B visa itself), which firms, for how long, and on what evidence, since Al Jazeera's headline calls them fraud claims. The mechanism: an employer sponsors the worker, so the penalty falls on the company's name but lands on the employees, most of them Indian, whose legal status depends on a pending application; say how many are affected, what happens to applications already filed, what role the vice-president's office played (he is tagged), and what Microsoft and the Indian firms replied. Every accusation is an allegation. The structural point: the US tech industry's workforce is built on a pipeline the executive can close firm by firm without Congress. Write from Al Jazeera, Dawn and the Telegraph text on Yahoo (the AP report is at apnews.com/article/h1b-visa-program-vance-microsoft-e7b3a407f822702b269ee277d21343ea); TRT World is Turkish state media, but the independent sources lift the label. Dateline Washington. US dateline (1 of 3).

stories.label: US proposes $100,000 charge for international students to do post-graduate work
stories.summary: A rule proposed by the Department of Homeland Security would put a $100,000 price on a science job after graduation for international students in the United States, and would make the university, not the employer, pay it. Lead with the sum and who is billed. The mechanism: say what Optional Practical Training is (the work period a student visa allows after a degree, longer for science and engineering graduates), how many people use it each year and from which countries, what the fee attaches to and when the comment period closes, and that this is a proposal, not a rule in force. Say why Nature's report tags the Palestinian territories, if the page explains it. Who it lands on: graduates from India, China, Iran, Pakistan and the rest of the Global South for whom this is the bridge to a research career, and the laboratories that run on them. Mention in one clause the same day's suspension of Microsoft and other firms from green card sponsorship, a separate measure covered separately. Single source, Nature's news desk. Dateline Washington. US dateline (2 of 3).

stories.label: Brazil's Flavio Bolsonaro vows to keep pension increases above inflation rate
stories.summary: The site has not yet reported Brazil's election, so lead with the result and put the pledge second: Flavio Bolsonaro, the right-wing senator and son of the former president, unexpectedly finished first in Sunday's first round and faces a runoff later this month; on Thursday he promised to keep raising pensions above inflation if he wins. Give the first-round shares, his opponent and the runoff date as Reuters does. The mechanism: the pledge is a candidate of the right adopting the left's most expensive policy, so say what the pension rule is (benefits tied to a minimum wage that rises faster than prices), what it costs the budget, what his own economic team and the markets had expected him to say, and how his rival answered. Be plain that it is a campaign promise, not a decision. Who it lands on: tens of millions of Brazilian pensioners, and a government whose debt cost depends on whether investors believe either candidate will restrain spending. Single source, Reuters. Dateline São Paulo.

stories.label: Rising food prices and poor rains fuel fears of hunger crisis in Darfur
stories.summary: Food prices are rising and the rains have failed across Darfur as the harvest should be starting, and Radio Dabanga's correspondents report fears of a wider hunger crisis, beginning in West Darfur. Lead with the prices the report gives (a sack of sorghum or millet now against a few months ago, in named markets) and the localities it names. The mechanism: hunger here is made by the war as much as by the weather, so say who controls the areas described (the Rapid Support Forces hold most of Darfur), how displacement and the destruction of farms cut planting, what the poor rains did to what was planted, and what blocks food and aid from arriving (roads, fees at checkpoints, the Chad border), only as the report gives it. Who it lands on: displaced families and farmers, named and quoted where Dabanga does. Give any famine classification or caseload figure only with its source. Radio Dabanga is the regional outlet and the only source. Dateline the West Darfur town the report names (El Geneina if it does).

stories.label: Life in Iran's War-Torn South on the Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: A ground report from Hormozgan, the Iranian province on the Strait of Hormuz: the fish market in Bandar Abbas, the graves of schoolchildren in Minab, and a wedding bombed in Kuhestak, where residents say the ceasefire never arrived. The site has covered the strait as traffic counts and crude prices all week; this is the people who live on its shore. Lead with the most specific fact the reporter witnessed or documented: the strike on the wedding, with its date, the dead and who residents and officials say carried it out, each attributed. Then the mechanism of daily life under blockade: what has happened to fishing, to the port and to prices in Bandar Abbas, and what the Minab deaths were. Name victims where the piece does and count the dead with their source. It is reportage, so write it as a report of what was found, not a travel narrative, and state no attribution of a strike the piece does not support. Ship traffic through the Strait of Hormuz gets one clause. Single source; no regional outlet in the feed. Dateline Bandar Abbas.

stories.label: WTO hikes global trade growth forecast, says Pakistan among nations benefitting from trade disruption amid ME conflict
stories.summary: The World Trade Organisation sharply raised its forecast for 2026 goods trade, crediting the boom in AI hardware, and found that some countries, Pakistan among them, are gaining from the disruption the Middle East war has caused. Lead with the surprising half: a war that closed a strait has made winners. The mechanism: say what the old and new growth figures are, how much of the increase is chips, servers and the equipment for data centres, and exactly how Pakistan benefits as the WTO describes it (the concept tags point to fertiliser; diverted orders and overland routes if the report says so), and which countries lose. Then the caveat the WTO itself gives about what a longer closure of Hormuz would do. A forecast is a forecast: mark it as one. Who it lands on: Pakistani exporters and farmers on one side, the import-dependent economies paying for rerouted cargo on the other. Dawn is the regional outlet and the only source. Dateline Geneva, where the WTO published, or Islamabad as Dawn files it.

stories.label: China defends yuan policy as EU ups pressure over ballooning deficit
stories.summary: China said on Thursday it has never pursued competitive depreciation of the yuan, answering European policymakers who want a stronger Chinese currency to shrink a record Chinese trade surplus and the EU's widening deficit with it. Lead with the exchange: who in Beijing said it (the People's Bank of China or the foreign ministry, as the report gives it) and which European officials are pressing (trade commissioner Maroš Šefčovič is tagged). The mechanism: say where the yuan trades against the euro and the dollar and how far it has moved, how the central bank steers it through the daily fixing, how large China's surplus and the EU's deficit now are, and what Brussels can actually do if Beijing does not move (tariffs, anti-subsidy cases). Name the series plainly: the yuan and the euro. Who it lands on: European manufacturers competing with cheaper Chinese exports, and Chinese exporters who depend on the rate. The feed entry was a short Reuters teaser carried by Nikkei: write only what the fetched page supports. Single source. Dateline Beijing.

stories.label: Fading control over 'jumping genes' may explain why big dogs age faster
stories.summary: Across mammals bigger species live longer, from two years for a mouse to nearly 200 for some whales, yet within dogs the rule runs backwards: large breeds die years before small ones. A new study ties this to transposable elements, the 'jumping genes' that make up a large part of the genome, which large dogs lose the ability to keep silent as they age. Lead with the paradox and the finding. The mechanism for a technical reader: say what transposons are and how cells normally suppress them (DNA methylation and related silencing), what the researchers measured, in how many dogs of which sizes and in which tissues, how the loss of control differed by body size, and why active transposons would speed ageing (DNA damage, inflammation). State the limits: an association, and whether anything was tested causally. Name the journal and the lead institution. The feed entry was a teaser: write only what the fetched page supports. Give the article a dateline and location: the city of the lead authors' institution as the page states it.

stories.label: Amazon builds 1,000th satellite, is weeks away from space Internet rollout
stories.summary: Amazon has built its 1,000th broadband satellite and says commercial service from low-Earth orbit is weeks away, which would give Starlink its first competitor at scale. Lead with the two numbers that matter and are not the same: satellites built against satellites actually in orbit, and how many the constellation needs before coverage is continuous. The mechanism for a technical reader: say what has held Amazon back (launch capacity, with Vulcan Centaur tagged, and which rockets it has bought), the regulator's deadline to deploy half the constellation and whether Amazon will meet it, where service starts first and at what speeds and terminal price, as Ars gives it. The structural point: satellite internet for much of the Global South is today a single company owned by one man, and this week India's government and Elon Musk argued over who controls that connection (covered 10-08, one clause). Single specialist source. Give the article a dateline and location: the place Ars gives for the factory or the announcement (Kirkland, Washington, if it names the plant). US dateline (3 of 3).

stories.label: The Exploration Company to Test Lunar Hopper Demonstrator in 2027
stories.summary: The Exploration Company, the Franco-German startup building Europe's first private cargo capsule, will test a one-tonne lunar 'hopper' demonstrator called ONEIROS in the United Arab Emirates in 2027, paid for with private money. Lead with the test and where it happens: a European lunar vehicle flown in the Emirates, not in Europe. The mechanism for a technical reader: say what a hopper is (a lander that takes off again and flies short arcs between sites), what the demonstrator will prove (a throttleable methane-fuelled engine, guidance for repeated landings), why methane, and how it connects to the company's Nyx capsule and to a later lunar lander. Say why the UAE, as the report gives it (test range, regulation, an Emirati partner or investor), and what the company claims about cost per kilogram to the lunar surface, as a claim. The structural point: Gulf money and territory are becoming part of Europe's route to the Moon. Single specialist source; no regional outlet in the feed. Dateline the UAE site if the page names it, otherwise Abu Dhabi.

stories.label: Ed Miliband insists UK will 'build back up' presence in Jerusalem as British consulate closes on Israel's orders
stories.summary: Israel has removed the signage of Britain's consulate in occupied East Jerusalem and announced that 20 British diplomats, including the consul general, must leave; London says it will keep and 'build back up' its presence. Lead with the removal and the expulsions, then what each government says the status now is (closed, or downgraded), quoted exactly. The mechanism: the consulate is Britain's mission to the Palestinians, not to Israel, and it sits in territory Britain regards as occupied, so say what the consulate does (the West Bank, Gaza, aid, consular work), what Israel gives as its reason (Gideon Sa'ar is tagged) and which British decision it is retaliating for, and what the Vienna Convention lets an occupying power do to a third state's mission there, only as the reports give it. Who it lands on: Palestinians in East Jerusalem and the West Bank who lose a diplomatic witness, more than the diplomats. Who is speaking for London and in what office: give Ed Miliband's title as the reports do. Al Jazeera and Middle East Eye are the regional outlets, Dawn the third. Dateline East Jerusalem.

stories.label: 33 killed in Russian bomb attack on bus stop in Ukraine's stronghold
stories.summary: A new attack, separate from the strikes covered this morning (38 dead on both sides, one clause): a Russian bomb hit a bus stop in Kramatorsk, the largest city Ukraine still holds in Donetsk Oblast, killing civilians waiting for transport. Lead with the dead and where they were standing. The toll moved through the day (an early Al Jazeera count was 12, later reports say 33): give the latest figure the fetched pages support and attribute it to the authority that gave it. The mechanism: say what weapon was used (a glide bomb, if the reports say so), how far Kramatorsk is from the front, and why the city matters as the hub of what remains of Ukrainian-held Donbas; then the European Commission's statement that perpetrators of war crimes must be held accountable, and Moscow's account if any is reported. Name victims where the reports do. Ukrainska Pravda is a Ukrainian outlet: take the count and the scene from the New York Times and Al Jazeera as well. Dateline Kramatorsk.

stories.label: Democrats sue US President Trump over taxpayer-funded ad campaign
stories.summary: The Democratic National Committee has sued Donald Trump over television advertisements paid for with public money that it says promote his political programme, less than four weeks before the 3 November midterms. Lead with the suit: the court, the defendants, which ads and which agencies paid for them, and the sum, as the report gives it. The mechanism: say which laws the complaint relies on (the ban on using appropriated funds for publicity or propaganda, the Hatch Act, if named), what the White House says the ads are for, and what the court is asked to order and how fast it could rule before the vote. Accountability is the point: public funds used as campaign funds, checked only if a party sues. Every claim in the complaint is an allegation. Single source. Dateline Washington. US dateline (1 of 3).

stories.label: Asaba Massacre: Obasanjo urges forgiveness, reconciliation
stories.summary: At the commemoration of the 1967 Asaba massacre, in which Nigerian federal troops killed hundreds of civilian men and boys during the civil war, former president Olusegun Obasanjo asked survivors and families to forgive and said 'never again'; the Asagba of Asaba, Epiphany Azinge, answered that the Odi killings of 1999 happened under Obasanjo's own presidency. Lead with that exchange, quoted exactly. The mechanism: say what happened in Asaba in October 1967 and who commanded the troops, what the state has and has not done since (no prosecution, what apology or inquiry, what memorial), what happened at Odi, and what the community is asking for now, as the report gives it. The structural point: a state that asks victims to forgive without naming who gave the orders. Give death tolls with their source, since estimates differ. Premium Times is the regional outlet and the only source. Dateline Asaba.

stories.label: ECB Officials Took 'Proporionate' Step With Last Month's Hike
stories.summary: The European Central Bank's account of its 9-10 September meeting shows officials judged last month's rate rise a 'proportionate' step that still does not restrict growth, and Reuters reports the bank is expected to raise again in December with euro-zone inflation at almost double its 2% target. Lead with the account and the inflation figure. The mechanism: say what the ECB's policy rate is now and where it was before the rise, what is driving prices (energy, with oil above $100 since the Hormuz crisis), why officials think policy is not yet restrictive, and what the account says about the next move; mark December as an expectation, not a decision. Name the series plainly: the ECB's policy rate and the euro. Who it lands on: euro-zone borrowers and the governments with the heaviest debts, France first (the ECB's refusal to intervene in French bonds was covered 10-07, one clause). Bloomberg may be paywalled: write from Reuters and use Bloomberg only for what the fetched page gives. Dateline Frankfurt.

stories.label: India Set for Back-to-Back Rate Hikes as Inflation Risks Mount
stories.summary: The Reserve Bank of India raised its repo rate to 5.5% on 7 October, its first increase since 2023, and economists at Goldman Sachs, Standard Chartered and Deutsche Bank now expect it to raise again at successive meetings into next year. Lead with the decision, which the site has not yet reported, and put the forecasts second and as forecasts. The mechanism: say what pushed the bank to move (broadening price pressures, imported energy with crude above $100, the rupee), what the governor said about the path ahead, and how the vote split, as the BBC and Bloomberg give it. Who it lands on: Indian households with floating-rate home loans and small businesses, and a government that borrows heavily; give the inflation figure and the bank's target. The structural point: India joins the Fed and the ECB in a tightening cycle driven by a war it is not party to. Bloomberg may be paywalled: write from the BBC and use Bloomberg only for what the fetched page gives. Dateline Mumbai, where the Reserve Bank sits.

stories.label: GST Council proposes 5% tax option for passenger transport, vehicle rentals using EVs- Moneycontrol.com
stories.summary: India's GST Council, the body of federal and state finance ministers that sets the national goods and services tax, has voted to strip tax officials of their power to arrest, raise the threshold for criminal prosecution fivefold, and automate refunds. Lead with the arrest power, not the rate changes: a tax authority giving up the power to jail the people it audits. The mechanism: say what the power was and how it was used against traders and small firms, what the old and new prosecution thresholds are in rupees, how the automated refund works and how long refunds took before, and from what date each change applies; the 5% option for electric-vehicle passenger transport and rentals goes in one sentence. Who it lands on: the millions of small businesses for which a GST notice meant the threat of custody, and state governments that depend on the revenue. Say what critics or state ministers objected to, if the reports give it. Two Indian sources, Rediff and Moneycontrol. Dateline New Delhi.

stories.label: Argenx sees unusual setback with failure of late-stage study of drug for autoimmune disease
stories.summary: Argenx says its blockbuster drug Vyvgart did no better than placebo in a Phase 3 trial in people with Sjögren's disease, a chronic autoimmune condition with no approved disease-modifying treatment. Lead with the result. The mechanism for a technical reader: say how the drug works (it blocks the FcRn receptor so the body clears IgG antibodies faster, which is why it works in antibody-driven diseases such as myasthenia gravis), what the trial measured and in how many patients, what the earlier mid-stage data had shown, and what a clean failure says about whether Sjögren's is driven by those antibodies at all; note what it means for other companies testing FcRn blockers in the same disease, only as STAT reports it. Who it lands on: patients, mostly women, who remain without a treatment. The share-price reaction is one clause at most. Single specialist source. Give the article a dateline and location: the city the page gives for the company (Amsterdam, where Argenx is registered, if none is given); not a US dateline.

stories.label: Medellín went green to stay cool – heat rose faster
stories.summary: Medellín's 'green corridors', the tree-planting programme that made Colombia's second city a global model for cooling a city cheaply, have been outpaced: temperatures rose faster than the trees could offset as the climate warmed and the city kept building. Lead with the measurement the report gives: how much cooling the corridors delivered where they were planted, against how much the city as a whole has warmed, and over what years. The mechanism for a technical reader: shade and evapotranspiration cool a street locally, while the urban heat island grows with every hectare of new concrete and with regional warming, so say which studies or city data the piece cites, where the hottest districts are (the informal hillside neighbourhoods have the fewest trees), and what researchers and officials now propose instead. The structural point: a fix celebrated and copied abroad was a local remedy for a problem that scales with the city. Give figures only as the page does and name the institutions behind them. Single specialist source. Dateline Medellín.

stories.label: India defends satellite internet approval process after Elon Musk jab
stories.summary: India's government has rejected Elon Musk's claim that 'oligarchs' are blocking Starlink, saying its satellite-internet approvals follow the law; Musk replied by asking whether Mukesh Ambani is 'the real boss of India'. Lead with what is actually stuck, not the insult: which licence or clearance Starlink holds, which it still lacks (spectrum allocation, security clearance, pricing), and since when. The mechanism for a technical reader: say how India assigns satellite spectrum (administratively, not by auction, which Reliance Jio and Airtel lobbied against), what the security conditions are (local gateways, lawful interception, data kept in India), and that Jio and Airtel are both Starlink's rivals and its announced distributors. The structural point: a foreign billionaire and a domestic one contest who controls the last-mile connection of 1.4 billion people, and the regulator is the only party neither owns. Quote both sides exactly and state neither's charge as fact. RT is Russian state media: take facts from Al Jazeera and India Today. Dateline New Delhi.

stories.label: Over 6 million bitcoin sit behind exposed public keys as AI warnings mount
stories.summary: More than 6 million bitcoin, close to a third of all that will ever exist, sit at addresses whose public keys are already visible on the blockchain, CoinDesk reports. Lead with the number and say at once what it is not: a measure of address usage, not of an attack, and no practical break of bitcoin or ether wallet keys has been demonstrated. The mechanism for a technical reader: a bitcoin address normally publishes only a hash of the public key, and the key itself is revealed when coins are spent from it or when an old pay-to-public-key or reused address is involved; an attacker who could derive a private key from a public one (the elliptic-curve discrete-log problem, which a large quantum computer running Shor's algorithm would solve) could take those coins and no others. Say who produced the count, how the exposed coins break down (early mined coins, exchange cold wallets, reused addresses), what the 'AI warnings' in the headline actually claim, and what migration to quantum-resistant signatures would require of holders and of the protocol. Name the series plainly: the price of bitcoin, in one clause. Single source. Give the article a dateline and location: the city of the firm that produced the data if the page gives it, otherwise New York, where CoinDesk is based. US dateline (2 of 3) in that case.

stories.label: Hackers target two South Korean megachurches, potentially exposing congregant data
stories.summary: Two of South Korea's largest Protestant churches are investigating cyberattacks that may have exposed personal details, financial records and internal documents of hundreds of thousands of members. Lead with the scale and name the churches as The Record does (Yoido Full Gospel Church is pictured). The mechanism for a technical reader: say how the intruders got in and whether it was ransomware or theft for sale, who claimed it, what was taken, and what the churches and South Korea's privacy regulator have said. The structural point: a megachurch holds what a bank and a membership registry hold together (identity, donations, family and pastoral records) with a fraction of the security budget and, in most countries, lighter regulation; say what Korean law requires of a religious body after a breach, only as the report gives it. Who it lands on: congregants whose religious affiliation and giving are now potentially exposed. The feed entry was a teaser: write only what the fetched page supports. Single specialist source. Dateline Seoul.
